bull.b: Sustained TTM free cash flow of roughly $4.4B that closely tracks reported earnings signals high earnings quality and durable cash conversion. This level of cash generation supports organic investment, share repurchases and debt servicing, giving management long-term strategic flexibility across cycles.

Very high adjusted EBITDA margins (~85%) reflect strong operating leverage and efficient monetization in the ad platform. Durable high margins provide capacity to invest in AI/creative tooling, return capital, and absorb cyclical ad-market swings, strengthening long-term cash generation and ROI on product investments.

Opening Axon as a global self-serve product is a structural expansion of addressable market and advertiser access. A scalable self-serve platform reduces sales friction, increases customer velocity and lifetime monetization potential, and can compound revenue sustainably if onboarding and creative supply scale as planned.

bear.b: Debt-to-equity of roughly 1.5x, while improved, keeps financial leverage meaningfully above lower-debt peers. Elevated leverage raises sensitivity to earnings declines or higher rates, constrains capital allocation optionality for M&A or buybacks, and increases refinancing risk during cyclical slowdowns.

Material swings in revenue growth across recent years reduce predictability of cash flows and complicate multi-year planning. Volatility increases execution risk for scaling new verticals and raises the chance margins or FCF conversion could deteriorate if new products underperform or advertising demand softens.

Dependence on external AI models and cloud GPU capacity introduces recurring cost pressure and vendor exposure as creative generation scales. Higher compute costs act as a structural 'tax' on margins and, combined with onboarding breakage, could slow customer ramp and reduce the durability of margin expansion if not mitigated.
